response.answer: For MNAR, pattern-mixture models are used; for selection bias, selection models; for measurement error, latent-reliability models. These algorithms adjust CI tests and edge inclusions by accounting for missing data, bias, and error.

results.content: However, while we know software engineers express sentiment and emotions, we do not know how these expressions affect the software development process. In this thesis, we study expressions of sen-timent and emotions, and specifically, we study three aspects of sentiment and emotions in software engineering: Theory, Tools, and Practice. Through studying the tools used to classify sentiment and emotions in software engineering texts, we find small differences in performance scores between contemporary machine-learning tools and recently released deep-learning tools. results.content: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have showcased impressive code generation capabilities, primarily evaluated through language-to-code benchmarks. In this paper, we explore alternative way of leveraging Large Language Model (LLM) generated feedback to address the inherent limitation of using human-labeled data. Recent research in federated large language models (LLMs) has primarily focused on enabling clients to fine-tune their locally deployed homogeneous LLMs collaboratively or on transferring knowledge from server-based LLMs to small language models (SLMs) at downstream clients. As large language models (LLMs) continue to advance, accurately and comprehensively evaluating their performance becomes increasingly challenging. Our analysis demonstrates that this task is highly challenging, with large language models (LLMs) yielding unsatisfactory performance. In this paper, we propose a data augmentation method via lightweight large language model (LLM) generation and tree hybridization. The recent emergence of various large language models, which can be fine-tuned with minimal instruction data, has demonstrated impressive performance across various tasks.
